rename.resolution: Re-verdicted 2026-09-04; the premise was wrong. Note the symbol is not even linkable in a default build — `nros_cpp_publisher_loan` is `#[cfg(feature = "lending")]` while cbindgen emits it unconditionally (issue 0814).

why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-04 from `rename`. The row argued that "in C++ both sides return a typed RAII handle … so unlike the C API there is no shape difference here to justify the different verb". The word TYPED is false, and it was the whole argument.

rclcpp's `borrow_loaned_message()` takes NO arguments and returns `LoanedMessage<T>` whose `get()` yields `MessageT&`. Ours is `Expected<Loan> loan(size_t requested_len)` (`publisher.hpp:171`) over a byte span: `uint8_t* data()` (`:121`), `Result commit(size_t actual_len)` (`:128`). A byte token sized by an explicit caller-supplied length is precisely the shape this row said applies only to C — and `cpp:LoanedMessage` in this same file already says so ("Ours is `Publisher::Loan`"), as do all four C and Rust loan rows, which carry `divergence`. Two rows described one object and disagreed about whether it was typed.

The constraint is RFC-0010 D7 and issue 0814: the lent slot is `len` BYTES because CDR length is not known before encoding, and upstream's loan carries a `rosidl_message_type_support_t*` that this ABI declines. Giving a byte token rclcpp's typed name would be a worse divergence than the verb is.
